summary.one_liner: A native macOS menu bar Shadowsocks client for Apple Silicon Macs that manages servers, subscriptions, and routing rules and exposes local SOCKS5 and HTTP proxies.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes ShadowsocksX-NG2, a rewrite of the ShadowsocksX-NG Shadowsocks client, which runs from the menu bar. It lets you add or import Shadowsocks configurations, group servers, mark favorites, and add HTTPS SIP-008 subscriptions that show traffic and expiry info. Routing can be set to global, rules, or direct mode, with presets for GFW List destinations and mainland China destinations plus custom rules. It supports SIP022 AEAD-2022 and SIP023 ciphers and load balancing through upstream sslocal, and can test server latency. Mac apps and LAN devices can connect through local SOCKS5 and HTTP proxies, with optional LAN listeners (off by default) and access credentials. It bundles v2ray-plugin and Cloak, and the server library is encrypted on disk with age.
use_cases: Manage multiple Shadowsocks servers from the Mac menu bar
Import Shadowsocks configs from SIP-008 subscription links
Route GFW-blocked or mainland China traffic through a proxy
Share a Mac's proxy with LAN devices via SOCKS5 or HTTP
Run Shadowsocks with v2ray-plugin or Cloak obfuscation
how_to_run: Download the latest ShadowsocksX-NG2 release from GitHub Releases
stack: Swift (macOS app, inferred from native Mac client)
notable: Native Apple Silicon menu bar client with Simplified Chinese and English UI
SIP-008 subscription support showing traffic and expiry data
Bundled v2ray-plugin with a Hysteria2 transport mode for Shadowsocks TCP
Local SOCKS5 and HTTP proxies that can be shared to LAN devices with credentials
Server library and listener config encrypted on the Mac with age; diagnostic reports redact secrets
caveats: Requires macOS 15 or later and an Apple Silicon (arm64) Mac
NG2 is still in development; the legacy 1.x version is no longer maintained
New issues and PRs are temporarily restricted until v2 is stable; use Discussions instead
Provides only the client, not servers or subscription services
